usageNotes: Use this endpoint to execute QEMU Guest Agent (QGA) commands against a running VM that has the guest agent installed and active. The VM must be powered on and the guest agent daemon must be running inside the guest OS; calls will fail with an error if the agent is unreachable. Commands are synchronous and return a `result` object immediately — no UPID is issued. The `fsfreeze-freeze` / `fsfreeze-thaw` pair is commonly used before and after live snapshots to ensure filesystem consistency.

tips: Before taking a live snapshot, call `fsfreeze-freeze` then immediately call `fsfreeze-thaw` after the snapshot completes to avoid leaving the guest filesystem in a frozen state.
`ping` is the cheapest way to verify the guest agent is responsive before issuing more impactful commands.
`shutdown` via QGA is a clean OS-level shutdown (equivalent to pressing the power button inside the OS), unlike the forceful ACPI or stop calls available through other endpoints.
`suspend-disk` (hibernate), `suspend-ram` (suspend-to-RAM), and `suspend-hybrid` depend on guest OS support — they will error on guests that lack the capability.
The caller needs the `VM.GuestAgent.Unrestricted` privilege on `/vms/{vmid}` — a standard API token scoped to a single VM is sufficient.
